normative_extracts.quote: A state machine defines a finite set of states and explicit transitions triggered by events, ensuring only valid state-event pairs execute.
Modeling UI flows as finite states eliminates impossible boolean flag combinations such as isLoading && isError.

engine_internals.mechanism_summary: Replaces N overlapping boolean flags (2^N states) with a discriminated union of valid states and an explicit (state, event) -> nextState transition table.

production_failures.symptom: Payment form submits twice when user double-clicks Pay during a slow API call
production_failures.root_cause: Submit handler only checked !isLoading in an async closure before state updated, instead of locking transitions out of the 'submitting' state.
production_failures.mitigation: Model the form as a finite state machine where SUBMIT is only handled in 'idle' or 'error', and ignored in 'submitting'.

production_failures.symptom: UI renders both a loading spinner and an error banner simultaneously
production_failures.root_cause: Independent booleans isLoading and hasError were updated separately; retry set isLoading=true without resetting hasError=false.
production_failures.mitigation: Replace boolean flags with a single status discriminant ('idle' | 'loading' | 'success' | 'error').
